reason: Verified against the real merged catalog (2026-08-20): each component ships as its own independently-installable package on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora, while Flathub bundles the whole suite into one flatpak (which the match tiers already correctly group alongside deb/Fedora's own bare libreoffice metapackage, via exact normalized-name matching).

Same shape as LibreOffice. Deliberately narrower than every calligra-named package in the real catalog: Void Linux fragments Calligra into many packaging artifacts (32-bit variants, -devtools, -handbook, -libs, -plugins, -extras, -data subpackages) that fail the keep.ndjson litmus test (a user wouldn't launch these on their own) and are excluded from this list; dev.geopjr.Calligraphy is a genuinely different, unrelated calligraphy-practice app that happens to share the name prefix and must never be confused with this suite.

User-reported: these are browser extensions bundled/packaged for Zen specifically (AUR-only, zen-browser-<extension> naming), not standalone apps -- same shape as LibreOffice/Calligra (a main app plus separately-installable components), not filter/rules.ts noise, since a user might genuinely search for a Zen Browser extension by name and should land on the real Zen Browser app rather than nothing. zen-browser-twilight-bin deliberately excluded -- Twilight is a distinctly branded separate release channel (Zen's nightly/beta), not an extension, and not conflated with stable Zen here.
